newsitem.title: USA: Metro One sees erratic earnings in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Metro One sees erratic earnings in 1997.

text.p: Metro One Telecommunications' rapid expansion into new markets will likely result in an erratic earnings performance in 1997 before it gets on a track of steady earnings growth in 1998, President and Chief Executive Officer Timothy Timmins said.
"As we go through the investment and pain of opening more call centers, we could see our earnings bopping around," Timmons told the Cruttenden Roth Growth Stock Conference here.
"But we are taking these steps now to make sure we can bank on earnings in the end," he said.
Metro One provides enhanced directory assistance services to telephone, particularly wireless, users.
In 1997 it plans to expand into major markets including New York, San Francisco, Los Angeles, Dallas, Boston and Kansas City.

Under the contracts it enters with phone companies, users access its services under the familiar "411" or "555-1212" numbers, but are given additional services such as message leaving options and more content for customers needing further assistance.

Timmins said the company's plan to open more local call centers around the U.S. was crucial to its strategy of building a staff of people who would be familiar with all the different regions of the country, and better able to serve callers in those different regions.
